<reason>CON won by breaking PRO's mitigation asymmetry. PRO conceded the name releases over objection with only contact limits after, and only proven specific threat delays release. CON showed that sequence is decisive: a no-contact order cannot unrelease a name from spouse, later children, or search, while medical need can be partly met anonymously plus own testing. PRO never answered third-party spread, so its knowledge-with-boundaries claim collapsed.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's use of PRO's A1 admission in B4.1 — name prints even over objection, contact rules only after — paired with A2.7/A4.7 that a released name cannot be unreleased to spouse/family, which left PRO's privacy-after-knowledge mitigation without an answer.</best_rebuttal>
